prompt.brief: Design an SLA intelligence platform that computes service-level indicators and error budgets, predicts breaches across dependency chains, and coordinates proactive mitigation.
successSignals: Define SLI event contracts, SLO windows, availability/latency aggregation, exclusions, ownership, and composite dependency semantics.
Compute multi-window burn rates and remaining error budget, forecast breach risk, and avoid false certainty when samples are sparse or delayed.
Separate telemetry ingestion from query/alert paths; make rollups, SLO definitions, and forecast versions reproducible and replayable.
Explain alert deduplication, maintenance windows, remediation approvals, missing data, retention, observability, and degraded dashboards.

functional: Ingest request, latency, error, and dependency events; calculate SLI windows, SLO compliance, burn rates, and error budgets.
Expose service and composite-SLA dashboards with forecast confidence, freshness, drill-down evidence, and historical comparisons.
Create routed alerts and mitigation recommendations, support SLO changes/versioning, replay, and reconciliation after telemetry gaps.
nonFunctional: Update SLO aggregates within one minute and flag high-confidence breach risk at least 15 minutes ahead when evidence supports it.
Scale to millions of telemetry events per minute and large dependency graphs without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Millions of events/minute across 10k services and 100k dependency edges
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: SLI and error-budget correctness
points: Define request population, good-event rules, latency buckets, aggregation windows, and exclusion policy explicitly.
Keep event-time watermarks and late-data correction separate from dashboard freshness.
Version SLO changes so historical budget burn is not recomputed under a new objective.

deepDives.title: Dependency-chain prediction
points: Model ownership and dependency edges as versioned evidence, not an unbounded graph lookup at alert time.
Calibrate forecast confidence by service, horizon, incident class, and missing telemetry.
Distinguish a predicted breach from a confirmed SLO violation and show the evidence behind both.

deepDives.title: Safe proactive mitigation
points: Require policy, blast-radius, cooldown, and approval gates before any operational action.
Keep notification delivery and recommendation state independent from the SLI calculation commit.
Measure false positives, missed breaches, acknowledgement latency, and mitigation outcome.

tradeoffs.title: Exact windows versus approximate streaming
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use exact calculations for contractual SLOs and bounded approximations only for early warning or exploratory views.
tradeoffs.caution: An approximate burn rate must expose its error and cannot silently drive a contractual violation decision.

tradeoffs.title: Prediction versus threshold alerts
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep threshold alerts authoritative and use forecasts to prioritize investigation or approved prevention.
tradeoffs.caution: A forecast should not page or mutate production without confidence, evidence, and policy gates.

tradeoffs.title: Central topology versus local ownership
tradeoffs.recommendation: Centralize dependency discovery and freshness while letting service owners define SLI and SLO contracts.
tradeoffs.caution: A stale dependency graph can produce confident but incorrect chain forecasts.

commonMistakes: Calculating SLIs from dashboard aggregates without preserving raw event-time evidence.
Changing SLO policy in place and invalidating historical error-budget comparisons.
Treating a forecast as a confirmed breach or as permission for automatic remediation.
Ignoring missing telemetry and dependency-graph freshness in confidence scores.
Measuring alert volume without calibration, missed breaches, and mitigation outcomes.

followUps.question: How do you handle telemetry gaps?
followUps.answer: Mark affected windows incomplete, lower forecast confidence, backfill or replay from raw evidence, and avoid declaring a healthy SLO from missing data.

followUps.question: How do you prevent mitigation loops?
followUps.answer: Use recommendation and operation IDs, cooldowns, policy versions, blast-radius limits, expiry, and explicit approval for risky actions.

followUps.question: How do you prove a forecast was useful?
followUps.answer: Track calibrated probability, lead time, false positives, missed breaches, segment behavior, and whether approved mitigations changed the outcome.

rubric.description: The answer covers smart sla monitoring and prediction system telemetry, SLI/SLO windows, error budgets, dependencies, prediction, mitigation, and replay.
The answer separates event-time evidence, contractual SLO state, forecast confidence, and recommendation approval.
The answer makes mitigation policy-gated, auditable, bounded, and reversible where possible.
The answer measures telemetry gaps, freshness, calibration, page latency, and recovery after replay.
